t:
For compensation and expenses of officers and employees, as authorized by law, $172,249,000, including: for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Clerk, including not more than $13,000, of which not more than $10,000 is for the Family Room, for official representation and reception expenses, $21,911,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Sergeant at Arms, including the position of Superintendent of Garages, and including not more than $3,000 for official representation and reception expenses, $6,284,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer, $121,471,000, of which $7,806,000 shall remain available until expended; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Inspector General, $3,991,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Operations, $5,000,000, to remain available until expended; for salaries and expenses of the Office of General Counsel, $962,000; 
for the Office of the Chaplain, $161,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Parliamentarian, including the Parliamentarian and $2,000 for preparing the Digest of Rules, $1,767,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Law Revision Counsel of the House, $2,453,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Legislative Counsel of the House, $6,963,000; for salaries and expenses of the Office of Interparliamentary Affairs, $720,000; for other authorized employees, $161,000; and for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Historian, $405,000.

fable.w: This section only appropriates funds for salaries and expenses of House of Representatives offices such as the Clerk, Sergeant at Arms, and Chief Administrative Officer. The tempting reading is that phrases like "official representation and reception expenses" or "Interparliamentary Affairs" suggest outside engagement, but these are funding line items, not a process that brings non-federal parties into a federal decision. Every actor named is inside the federal government.
fable.s: For compensation and expenses of officers and employees, as authorized by law, $172,249,000

opus.w: This section only funds salaries and expenses for offices of the House of Representatives, such as the Clerk, Sergeant at Arms and Chief Administrative Officer, which are all inside the federal government. Nothing in it requires or allows outside parties to be consulted, to comment, to sit on an advisory body or to challenge a federal decision. References to 'reception expenses' or 'Interparliamentary Affairs' are just budget categories and set up no process involving outsiders.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** A tempting reading is that "official representation and reception expenses" or the "Office of Interparliamentary Affairs" means outsiders are involved with Congress. That reading fails. This section only appropriates money for salaries and expenses of offices inside the House of Representatives, which is part of the federal government. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue that would bring outside parties into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations clause detailing funding for the salaries and expenses of various offices within the U.S. House of Representatives. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. All actors mentioned are internal to the legislative branch.
qwen_chat.s: For compensation and expenses of officers and employees, as authorized by law, $172,249,000, including: for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Clerk... for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Sergeant at Arms... for salaries and expenses of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "official representation and reception expenses" imply interaction with the public or outside entities. However, these are internal administrative costs for congressional offices and do not constitute a statutory requirement for public participation, consultation, or coordination in a federal decision-making process. The text is purely an appropriations clause listing salaries and expenses for internal congressional offices.
